situation: We need to decide whether to replace our legacy payment system, but nobody on the product side knows its real failure history or what it costs to keep running.
recipient: The infrastructure lead who has operated this system for five years.
needed_back: Incident frequency over the last two years, annual maintenance effort in person-days, and the biggest risks of a cutover.
stress: single theme, three concrete asks - should NOT be over-grouped into headings

situation: We are scoping a mobile app rewrite and need to understand the current app across engineering, design, and support before committing to a plan.
recipient: The engineering manager who owns the existing app and also sits in on design and support reviews.
needed_back: Current architecture constraints, which design patterns are load-bearing, the top support complaints, and which of these would block a rewrite.
stress: many asks spanning distinct themes - requires ## theme grouping

situation: Our largest customer's contract renews in six weeks and we do not know which parts of the product they actually depend on.
recipient: The account manager who runs the relationship but is not technical.
needed_back: Which features they use daily, what they have complained about, and any commitments we have made that are not in the contract.
stress: non-technical recipient - Context paragraph must carry more background, no jargon

situation: We are choosing between two vector databases and the tradeoffs depend on how our retrieval workload actually behaves in production.
recipient: The staff engineer who built our retrieval pipeline and has benchmarked both databases already.
needed_back: Observed query latency distribution, index rebuild cost, and which database they would pick and why.
stress: expert recipient - over-explaining context is the failure mode

situation: A regulator has asked how we handle deletion requests and we cannot answer without knowing what our data pipeline actually retains and for how long.
recipient: The data platform engineer who owns the warehouse and the ingestion jobs.
needed_back: What personal data each pipeline stage retains, retention windows, whether deletion propagates downstream, and what would break if we shortened retention.
stress: invites compound questions - retention AND propagation must stay separate

situation: We are deciding whether to hire a dedicated SRE or spread on-call across the existing team, and the answer hinges on how bad on-call currently is.
recipient: The engineer who has carried the most on-call shifts this year.
needed_back: Above all, whether the current rotation is sustainable. Then page volume, how many pages were actionable, and what they would change first.
stress: explicit priority ordering - most-important-first is checkable

situation: Our onboarding flow drops 40% of signups and we do not know whether it is a UX problem, a verification problem, or an email deliverability problem.
recipient: The growth analyst who has the funnel instrumentation but has not been asked to look at this specific drop.
needed_back: Where exactly in the funnel users leave, whether the drop correlates with email provider or device, and what instrumentation is missing to tell these apart.
stress: answer requires the recipient to do work - How to answer must set effort and deadline

situation: Leadership wants us to adopt an internal AI coding assistant but we have no idea what would actually block adoption on the security side.
recipient: The security engineer who reviews all new third-party tooling.
needed_back: The review process and its timeline, the hard blockers versus negotiable concerns, and anything they have already rejected for similar reasons.
stress: unknown unknowns - the Anything else catch-all should earn its place
